tips.tip1: You can create a new task by clicking on any area of ​​the lists.
tips.tip2: Tasks can be dragged and dropped from one list to another or by changing their order.
tips.tip3: To rename a task, hover it and click the pencil (or double-click its text). To rename a list, double-click its name.
tips.tip4: To the right of the date of each list is the Snooze icon which allows you to send all the pending tasks of the current list to the next day.
tips.tip5: If you are not going to use the custom lists, you can hide them in the configuration menu.
tips.tip6: The calendar in the sidebar allows you to quickly scroll to a date.
tips.tip7: By placing the cursor on the name of the list, the Mark All icon will appear, this allows you to mark all the tasks that a list contains.
tips.tip8: You can create a new custom list using the Add New List button located on the side panel.
tips.tip9: The Start button places you on the current day.
tips.tip13: ITQ Todo stores the information on your computer. If you want to change your computer or browser, remember to create a backup. You can do it in the settings menu.
tips.tip14: Click and drag the central division to resize the height of the calendar and the custom lists. Double click on it to restore the size.
tips.tip15: You can modify the number of columns and the zoom of the application in the configuration panel.
tips.tip16: Click the three dots in the tasks to see details.
tips.tip17: You can drag and drop the sub task in the task details window.
tips.tip18: In the top of the task details window you can change the day or the list of a task.

people.name: People
people.summary: Keep track of who you are waiting on and who is waiting on you, straight from the text of your tasks.
people.s1: Write {'@'}name inside any task. Case and accents do not matter: {'@'}Mercedes, {'@'}mercedes and {'@'}Mercédes are the same person.
people.s2: Add #waiting (or #esperando, #blocked) to the task when you are waiting for that person.
people.s3: Add #owe (or #debo) when you owe them something, or start the task with a verb such as ask, send, reply, pregunta, manda or contesta.
people.s4: Open People from the sidebar or click a person's chip on any task. Each person gets three columns: waiting on them, you owe them, together.
people.s5: Click a task in People to jump straight to it. Only open tasks in active projects and in the last 30 days are counted.
people.tip: There is nothing to configure: mentions are read live, and the same name always groups into one person.

quick.name: Quick add and search
quick.summary: One box to search every task, add tasks with dates and run commands.
quick.s1: Press Ctrl+K (or /) from anywhere to open it.
quick.s2: Type to search all tasks in all lists. Click a tag to filter by it.
quick.s3: Start with + to add a task. It understands today, tomorrow, weekdays, dates like 22/11, times like 10am or 14:30, #tag, !1 !2 !3 for priority and /project to send it to a project.
quick.s4: Start with > to run commands, such as switching theme, closing the day or opening Mission control.
quick.tip: Press ? at any time to see all the keyboard shortcuts.

daily.name: Your day
daily.summary: Today is the home screen, and unfinished work follows you.
daily.s1: The app opens on Today. Press T to come back to it from any day, N to type a new task and the arrow keys to move between days.
daily.s2: Unfinished tasks from previous days move to today by themselves when you open the app and when the clock passes midnight with the app open. Turn it off in Settings with the option Automatically move old tasks.
daily.s3: Hover a task to see its buttons: the pencil renames it, the three dots snooze it (tomorrow, next Monday, any day) and the cross deletes it.
daily.s4: Click a task to complete it. Completed tasks sink to the bottom and new ones are added above them. Double-click the circle for focus mode.
daily.tip: Snoozing a project task keeps it in its project and also shows it on the day you picked.

projects.name: Projects and templates
projects.summary: Each project is its own list with notes, colour, a linked folder and trackers.
projects.s1: Create one from New Custom List in the sidebar and pick a template or a blank list.
projects.s2: Make your own templates: New Custom List, Create and edit templates, New template. Set its name, icon, colour and checklist, and drag the lines to reorder them. They appear next to the blank list.
projects.s3: Click a project title to open its Project crystal, with stats, the next deadline and the open tasks.
projects.s4: The three-dots menu of a project has notes, link folder (then click the folder icon to open it), export to markdown, the trackers and archive.
projects.s5: Archived projects are hidden from the board and from People. Use the link at the bottom of the board to show them.
projects.tip: Give the project a colour and every task you add to it inherits it.

batch.name: Batch tracker
batch.summary: Follow a long run of calculations, for example 60 singlepoints, as a single task.
batch.s1: In a project, open the three-dots menu and choose Batch tracker.
batch.s2: Pick a pending task, type how many calculations it covers and press Track.
batch.s3: Update how many have finished with -10, -1, +1, +10 or by typing the number. The bar and the percentage follow.
batch.s4: The task shows a done/total chip in the list. Click it to reopen the tracker. Remove batch stops tracking.

paper.name: Paper tracker
paper.summary: Plan a manuscript by sections, with the words you want and a conceptual draft.
paper.s1: In the project menu choose Paper tracker. Start from the article or computational template, or add your own sections.
paper.s2: For each section type the words written and the target you want. The bar shows progress, and the -100, +100 and +500 buttons help you update it.
paper.s3: Open Conceptual draft in a section to list its key points and tick them as the ideas settle. Progress averages words and concepts.
paper.s4: Optional, desktop app only: link the project folder, choose the .tex or .md manuscript and press Read words to fill the written words from its headings.
paper.s5: A chip with the overall percentage appears in the project header. Click it to reopen the tracker.
paper.tip: Headings found in the manuscript that are not in your plan appear as chips you can add with one click.

deadlines.name: Deadlines
deadlines.summary: Never lose a date: deadline chips, the list and the radar.
deadlines.s1: Open the three-dots menu of a task, choose Open details and set its deadline.
deadlines.s2: Tasks with a deadline show a chip with the date. Press D to see the upcoming ones.
deadlines.s3: The Deadline radar places them on rings by urgency: today, this week, this month, later. Hover a dot for details.
deadlines.tip: Tag a task paper, or just write the word paper in it, and the radar shows it as a paper deadline.

rhythm.name: Rhythm
rhythm.summary: See the whole picture, focus on one thing and close the week.
rhythm.s1: Mission control, in the sidebar, shows today, the next deadlines, meetings, what is pending and an activity heatmap.
rhythm.s2: Double-click the circle of a task for focus mode: just that task and a timer. Esc exits.
rhythm.s3: The daily and weekly summaries open by themselves at the right moment. You can reopen them from the search box with >.
rhythm.s4: On Fridays a Friday wrap-up appears in the sidebar and opens by itself after 17:00. Review what shipped and what carried over, and write the first thing for Monday.
